messages:
Sam: Quick question for the group — we're designing failover semantics when a customer's private control plane peering/PrivateLink degrades. TL;DR: how do we safely fail traffic to hosted control plane without losing audit continuity, while preserving least privilege and avoiding accidental data leakage? @Laura any thoughts?

Laura: My take: two-step, short-circuit approach. 1) Fast detection + mark tenant as `degraded` (read-only ops allowed), 2) Offer a controlled fallback path to hosted CP only if customer explicitly opts in (opt-in can be per-tenant or org-level). Emit audit events for every proxied call. Keep TTLs small so we can revert quickly.

Jing: Couple important cert/auth concerns: if we route to hosted CP we must NOT terminate customer mTLS with our cert and reissue without consent. Either 1) do an end-to-end mTLS hop (proxy tunnel passthrough) or 2) perform token rewrap with customer-approved KMS policy. Otherwise compliance flags will explode.

Matt: DNS failover is sticky — even low TTLs take time. Recommend health-check + explicit routing header + an active fallback flag in the route table. Example idea: a route policy blob:```json
{
  "tenant": "acme",
  "fallback": { "enabled": true, "require_admin_ack": false, "route_header": "X-CP-Fallback:hosted" },
  "ttl_seconds": 60
}
```This way dataplane can decide per-request.

Toni: From SRE POV, we need a clear incident and observability contract: when fallback flips we emit `cp.fallback.start` and `cp.fallback.end` events with masked KMS id and proof-of-acceptance token. Alerts: >5 min fallback = P2. Also add a metric `fallback.requests_per_min` and a histogram of latencies vs normal path.

security-bot: Policy reminder: any fallback that exposes stored user data to hosted infra must require one of: (a) tenant explicit opt-in, (b) legal review, or (c) audit flag enabled + 7d retention. Auto-rollouts are blocked while `fallback.active == true`.

Infra-bot: health-check output snapshot:```text
[1712349998] peering-status: degraded
[1712350030] tcp-probe: failed -> 3 retries
[1712350052] fallback-eval: eligible (opt-in=true)
```

Sam: Nice, that helps. To synthesize: 1) short TTL + health probes, 2) per-tenant opt-in gating, 3) explicit routing header and audit events, 4) never silently rewrap customer certs (must use pinned CA or KMS-approved rewrap), 5) SRE alerts on >5m. Next step: I'll spin up a small spike to implement the route-header + audit event flow and a test harness that simulates peering flaps. Who can pair for 1 day spike? @Matt @Jing?

Matt: I can take a half day to wire the routing header and health-check bits. Will mock behavior in the local relay.

Jing: I'll sketch the token-rewrap handshake and KMS policy constraints, plus a short threat model note.

Toni: I'll add the metrics and alert runbook draft. Quick ask — do we want a human approval gate for fallback->full-control-plane operations (e.g., model rollout)? seems prudent.

Sam: Yes, human approval for high-impact ops. We'll capture as part of the spike. I'll open a tiny RFC doc and link it here when done. Thanks all :thumbsup:
